name: NIKKOR Z 50mm f/1.8 S

focus.motor: Stepping motor (STM) with internal focusing, focus-by-wire control ring. Silent and accurate (Lenstip).
focus.notes: No AF/MF switch on the barrel. The single ring can be set to focus or to aperture/exposure compensation in the camera menu. Focus shift: OpticalLimits saw a small amount when stopping down (Z50, DX), Photography Life 'very minimal', and Phillip Reeve none visible (Z7 II).

stabilization.notes: No optical VR. Body IBIS on the Z8 and Z5 II. No stabilization on the Z50 II. Synchro VR needs lens VR, so it does not apply.

close_focus.notes: MFD 0.40 m from the focal plane, 0.15× (Nikon). That is not a close-up lens, so the effective-aperture loss at 0.15× is small (about 0.2 stop by the simple (1+m)² rule, a calculation, not a spec). Free working distance is not published and was not measured by any source found.

quick.headline: One of the sharpest 50s tested: f/1.8 is already excellent in the center, the whole frame peaks around f/2.8–f/4, and it stays sharp down to MFD.
quick.wide_open: Center is outstanding at f/1.8 (Lenstip Z7: over 70 lp/mm. Phillip Reeve Z7 II: 'phenomenal'). FX corners are only fair wide open. Lenstip had them a little below its decency level at f/1.8–f/2, reaching it near f/2.2, and Reeve rated them 'good'. Heavy FX vignetting wide open (Reeve 2.2 EV).

by_focal.wide_open_note: Lenstip (Z7, 45.7MP): center peak 83.7 lp/mm at f/4 (excellent-prime territory). DXOMARK (Z7): overall peak at f/2.8, 37 P-Mpix. Photography Life: slightly better at f/2.8 in the center on its second copy. Reeve (Z7 II): everything peaks at f/4 with excellent corners. Corners keep evening out to f/5.6 (DXOMARK: stopping down past the peak mainly improves uniformity).

quick.close_up_note: Phillip Reeve (Z7 II) tested close-up: very good at f/1.8, excellent from f/2.8 through f/11, and only very good at f/16 from diffraction. No visible focus shift or field-curvature issues were reported there. There is no reason to stop down far for close-ups: f/2.8–f/8 covers peak sharpness, chosen by depth of field.
quick.diffraction_note: DXOMARK (Z7, 45.7MP): diffraction starts to cut sharpness around f/5.6–f/8 and is most visible from f/11. OpticalLimits (Z50, DX 20.9MP): resolution drops from f/8 onward. Reeve: close-up f/16 falls from excellent to very good.
avoid: Avoid f/11–f/16 on the Z8 unless you need the depth of field.
Don't judge FX corners at f/1.8: stop to f/4 for edge-to-edge landscapes.
Don't expect smooth highlight bokeh in every scene: highlights can be defined, with faint onion rings and cat's-eyes off-center.
quick.confidence_reason: Lenstip (Z7), DXOMARK (Z7), Photography Life and Phillip Reeve (Z7 II) all agree on excellent f/1.8 center, peak f/2.8–f/4 and weaker FX corners wide open. Corner peak aperture is from Reeve plus DXOMARK's uniformity note, because the Lenstip FX-edge numbers are in an unreadable chart image.

character.bokeh: Smooth, soft backgrounds (OpticalLimits). Reeve: evenly lit bokeh balls without colored edges, faint onion-ring texture, cat's-eyes toward the corners ('Pass with Special Distinction'). Photography Life found highlights rather defined, not a sign of great bokeh. Lenstip: 'pleasing to the eye'.
character.flare_sunstar: Good flare resistance (Lenstip 'good', Reeve 'very good'). 9 rounded blades give 18-point sunstars, decent from f/11 and better at f/16 (Reeve).
character.ca: Lateral CA negligible: Lenstip 'negligible', Reeve 'virtually non-existent', DXOMARK about 1 px at f/1.8. LoCA: Lenstip 'moderate', OpticalLimits 'fairly low', Reeve 'negligible'.
character.distortion: Very low barrel: DXOMARK 0.2%, OpticalLimits about 0.4% (Z50 DX), Photography Life 0.57%, Lenstip 'invisible'.
character.vignetting: Strong on FX wide open: Reeve 2.2 EV at f/1.8, 1.3 EV at f/2.8, 0.9 EV from f/4. Photography Life up to 1.65 stops. Lenstip lists FX vignetting as its one con. Small on DX (OpticalLimits about ¾ stop on the Z50).
character.coma_astro: Reeve: very good at f/1.8 though not perfect, gone by f/2.8. Lenstip: no astigmatism problems. Usable for wide-open night shots with stars near center (inference).
character.focus_breathing: Reeve: none visible. Nikon lists the lens for movie focus-breathing compensation (camera feature). No source gave a number.
character.other: Weather-sealed, mostly metal barrel (Lenstip). Larger and heavier (415 g) than older F-mount 50/1.8s.

field_tips: Shoot f/1.8–f/2.8 for people and centered subjects without hesitation. The center is already excellent wide open.
For landscapes or groups across the frame, use f/4–f/5.6. FX corners only catch up there.
On the Z8 stay at f/8 or wider when you can. Diffraction shows from about f/5.6–f/8 and clearly from f/11.
Leave vignetting correction on, or plan to fix about 2 EV of corner falloff at f/1.8 in raw.
On the Z50 II it frames like a 75mm portrait lens with excellent edge-to-edge DX results from f/1.8, but there is no stabilization, so keep shutter speeds up.

body_notes.note: 45.7MP is what Lenstip, DXOMARK (Z7) and Reeve (Z7 II, 45.7MP) tested on. Peak f/2.8–f/4, with diffraction visible from about f/8 and clearly at f/11.
24.5MP: wide-open corner weakness and diffraction are less visible per pixel, so f/1.8–f/8 all look sharp and f/11 is fine (inference from pixel pitch).

DX (about 75mm-equivalent): uses only the strong central region. OpticalLimits on a Z50 (20.9MP DX): excellent across the frame from f/1.8, diffraction from f/8. Lenstip: very good DX edge, usable at f/1.8, about 65 lp/mm stopped down. No IBIS.

sources.name: Lenstip review: Nikon Nikkor Z 50 mm f/1.8 S (resolution and summary chapters)
sources.findings: Center over 70 lp/mm at f/1.8, peak 83.7 ±0.9 lp/mm at f/4 (decency level 42–44, excellent primes 80–85). DX edge usable at f/1.8–f/2, about 65 lp/mm stopped down. FX edge slightly below decency at f/1.8–f/2, reaching it near f/2.2. FX edge numbers only in a chart. Summary (https://www.lenstip.com/577.11-Lens_review-Nikon_Nikkor_Z_50_mm_f_1.8_S_Summary.html): sensational center, very good DX edge, acceptable FX edge, moderate LoCA, negligible lateral CA, invisible distortion, good against bright light, pleasing bokeh. Con: distinct vignetting on FX.

sources.name: DXOMARK: Nikon Nikkor Z 50mm F1.8 S lens review
sources.findings: Score 44. Sharpness 37 P-Mpix (Otus 55: 33). T1.9. Distortion 0.2% barrel. Lateral CA about 1 px at f/1.8. Sharpness good at f/1.8, peaks at f/2.8. Stopping down further mainly improves uniformity. Diffraction starts around f/5.6–f/8 and is most noticeable from f/11. Corner vignetting stays near −0.5 EV beyond f/4.

sources.name: Photography Life: Nikon Z 50mm f/1.8 S review (page 2)
sources.tested_on: Not stated on the page (chart values not readable)
sources.findings: 'One of the sharpest lenses we have ever tested'. Second copy slightly best at f/2.8 in the center. Barrel distortion 0.57%. Vignetting max 1.65 stops at infinity, largely gone by f/2.8. Very minimal focus shift. Bokeh highlights rather defined.

sources.name: Phillip Reeve: Review Nikon Nikkor Z 50mm f/1.8 S
sources.tested_on: Nikon Z7 II (45.7MP), plus Z fc and Z f samples
sources.findings: Infinity: center phenomenal wide open, mid almost excellent, corners good, all peaking at f/4 with excellent corners. Portrait distance: excellent across the zones. Close-up: very good at f/1.8, excellent f/2.8–f/11, very good at f/16 (diffraction). No focus shift. Coma very good at f/1.8, gone by f/2.8. Negligible LoCA and lateral CA. 18-point sunstars from f/11. Vignetting 2.2/1.3/0.9 EV at f/1.8/f/2.8/f/4. No visible distortion. No focus breathing. Bokeh: onion rings faint, cat's-eyes toward corners. Visual chart tests, not lab numbers.

sources.name: OpticalLimits: Nikkor Z 50mm f/1.8 S review (APS-C test)
sources.findings: Excellent resolution across the whole DX frame from f/1.8. Diffraction lowers results from f/8. Barrel distortion about 0.4% (about 0.16% corrected). Vignetting about ¾ stop wide open on DX. Lateral CA just under 0.3 px. Fairly low LoCA. Small focus shift on stopping down. Very smooth bokeh. Scores 10 optical, 9 build, 10 value. MTF values are in a chart image.

sources.name: Nikon: NIKKOR Z 50mm f/1.8 S product page
sources.findings: MFD 0.4 m. 0.15×. About 415 g. 62 mm filter. 9 rounded blades. 12 elements in 9 groups. f/16 minimum. No VR. Page mentions focus-breathing compensation for movies.

sources.name: Christopher Frost (YouTube): Nikkor Z 50mm f/1.8 S lens review with samples (Full-frame & APS-C)
sources.tested_on: Full-frame and APS-C Nikon Z bodies per the title (models not readable)
sources.findings: Only the title and channel were confirmed (YouTube oEmbed). Video, description and transcript could not be read, so none of his findings are used.

chris_frost.summary: The video exists: YouTube's oEmbed returns the title 'Nikkor Z 50mm f/1.8 S lens review with samples (Full-frame & APS-C)' with author 'Christopher Frost'. The watch page, description and transcript could not be fetched (client error), and no transcript or write-up was found by search. His verdict is unknown and is not used.

research_notes: 1) Center peak: Lenstip f/4 (83.7 lp/mm), DXOMARK f/2.8, Photography Life f/2.8, Reeve f/4. Recorded as f/2.8–f/4. The difference is about one stop and all were on 45MP bodies. 2) Corner peak f/4–f/5.6 relies on Reeve (excellent at f/4) and DXOMARK (uniformity improves past the peak). Lenstip FX-edge per-aperture values are in a chart image that could not be read. 3) OpticalLimits tested only on DX (Z50), so its 'excellent from f/1.8' applies to the DX frame and is not used for FX corners. 4) LoCA disagreement: Lenstip moderate, OpticalLimits fairly low, Reeve negligible. All say it is minor. 5) Distortion figures vary 0.2–0.57% by method. All say low. 6) Working distance at MFD is not published, so it is null. 7) Nikon's Z TC-1.4x compatibility list does not include this lens (checked for the MC 105 record), so tc_compatible is false.
